content.text:
The git line-history log directly shows the origin of the buggy code.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 004ec65b0c329e37ea592c764fd48f9ab9a44fe1

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I ran `git log -L` (line-history tracking) on the `setHalfwayBuffer` method in `sceAtrac3plus.java`, following the exact lines touched by the fix commit `9caec286` back through history. This directly shows every prior revision of those specific lines.

**(2) Root cause:** Commit `004ec65b` ("Wed Dec 12 18:22:54 2018") changed:
```java
inputBuffer = new pspFileBuffer(addr, bufferSize, readSize, readSize);
```
to:
```java
int maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap = bufferSize - ((bufferSize - info.inputFileDataOffset) % info.atracBytesPerFrame);
int maxSizeAfterFirstWrap = bufferSize - (bufferSize % info.atracBytesPerFrame);
inputBuffer = new pspFileBuffer(addr, maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap, maxSizeAfterFirstWrap, readSize, readSize);
```
This is exactly the code that `9caec286` removes/reworks. The new logic unconditionally aligned `maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap`/`maxSizeAfterFirstWrap` down to a multiple of `atracBytesPerFrame`, even when the buffer was not yet fully read (`readSize < bufferSize`) or when the aligned size would be smaller than `readSize` itself — producing an inconsistent/invalid buffer size relative to the actual data already read. The fix commit reintroduces the unaligned defaults (`bufferSize`/`bufferSize`) and only applies the alignment when `readSize < bufferSize` **and** the aligned value is still `>= readSize`, i.e., guards exactly the case the original 2018-12-12 change mishandled.

**(3) Evidence:** The `git log -L` output shows an unbroken lineage for these lines: `004ec65b` introduced the buggy alignment formulas, and no intermediate commit between `004ec65b` and `9caec286` touched these lines (the diff jumps straight from the buggy version to the fixed version). This is strong, direct evidence that `004ec65b` is the bug-introducing commit — there is minimal uncertainty here since the fix is essentially reverting/refining the precise lines added in that commit.
